From an idea to a first work plan

Fictional example, prepared to show the format of a deliverable. No client work, research, message sending or automation was performed by opening this page.

Fictional idea: a home-based design service helping local businesses prepare simple promotional materials.

Stage 1 / Define a useful first offer

Choose an initial audience and one clearly bounded service. Gather examples of what customers actually request. Treat the audience, pricing and demand as open questions until investigated.

Stage 2 / Agree the essentials

  • A business name and approved description.
  • A small website scope with enquiry and contact details.
  • Examples the business has permission to show.
  • A clear process for brief, quote, revision and acceptance.

Stage 3 / Prepare the first routine

Scope a small content batch, FAQ replies, enquiry tracking and an expense template. Choose the first work allowance instead of buying every department at once.

Stage 4 / Review before connecting

Approve the business accounts, file storage, sender identity and access limits. Start each connected workflow with an observable test and a clear failure path.

Your decisions

You approve the offer, business facts, spending, account access and customer-facing claims. The office supports agreed tasks; it does not establish legal permissions, guarantee demand or replace your business decisions.

Free trial versus paid scope

A short launch brief plus one other small deliverable may fit the limited free trial, subject to acceptance. A website, custom identity, full launch or connected automation requires a separate scope and agreement.
